title: SREV-005 PortRequest message header shape

carrier_shape.description: LPC/ALPC port-message carrier exposes DataLength on each chunk; LPC is emulated in ALPC on modern Windows

header_layout.description: MSG_HEADER carries ULONG length followed by a union of ULONG msgid or ULONG status; first chunk also carries a sequence byte at offset 3 of MSG_HEADER.length

minimum_length_gate.description: PipeServer::PortRequest must reject first chunks with msg->u1.s1.DataLength < sizeof(MSG_HEADER) before any msg_Data byte access

trust_order.description: Sequence-byte capture at offset 3, msgid read from msg_Data[1], length read from msg_Data[0], and buf_len/msgid/MAX_REQUEST_LENGTH validation all run only after the minimum-header gate succeeds

continuation_invariant.description: Existing chunk assembly protocol, sequence byte, request length checks, and service dispatch are unchanged

runtime_matrix.description: Windows runtime gate: malformed first chunks of length 0-7 never reach CallTarget; normal multi-chunk broker calls still work

contracts: PORT_MESSAGE carries u1.s1.DataLength giving received chunk byte count
MSG_HEADER is two ULONGs: length and union { msgid; status }
First chunk overlays a sequence byte at byte offset 3 of MSG_HEADER.length
PortRequest must compare DataLength against sizeof(MSG_HEADER) before touching msg_Data[0], msg_Data[1], or byte offset 3
First chunk acceptance requires nonzero msgid, nonzero buf_len, buf_len < MAX_REQUEST_LENGTH, buf_len >= sizeof(MSG_HEADER), buf_len >= DataLength
Continuation chunks reject when buf_len + DataLength exceeds the captured client->buf_hdr->length
